f.title: Apply the definition of unexpected adverse reaction
f.statement: An unexpected adverse reaction is an adverse reaction the nature or severity of which is not consistent with domestic labelling or market authorisation, or expected from characteristics of the drug.
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked. Relevant to section 2.3, which makes serious or unexpected ADRs to established drugs reportable.

f.title: Apply the seriousness criteria for a serious adverse event
f.statement: A serious adverse event is any event that is fatal; is life-threatening; is permanently or significantly disabling; requires or prolongs hospitalisation; causes a congenital anomaly; or requires intervention to prevent permanent impairment or damage.
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked. Relevant to section 2.3, which makes serious or unexpected ADRs to established drugs reportable. The criteria differ from ICH E2A (intervention to prevent permanent impairment instead of 'medically important').

rows.actor: Not named in source (applies to anyone assessing reportability)

A serious adverse event is any event that:
   • Is fatal
   • Is life-threatening
   • Is permanently/significantly disabling
   • Requires or prolongs hospitalization
   • Causes a congenital anomaly
   • Requires intervention to prevent permanent impairment or damage.
rows.review_note: Review: added; seriousness criteria determine reportability of ADRs to established drugs (2.3). Level Recommended (guideline definition). Double-check: definition only, no actor, level Recommended is a judgement. Note the criteria differ from ICH E2A: 'requires intervention to prevent permanent impairment or damage' replaces the 'medically important' criterion and the term used is 'serious adverse event'. Removed the statement's inferred link to 2.3 (moved to applicability). Quote is a bullet list.

f.title: Ensure suspected adverse reactions to own products are reported to the competent authority
f.statement: Pharmaceutical manufacturers, applicants and research organisations have to ensure that suspected adverse reactions to their products are reported to the competent authority.
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked.

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical manufacturers, applicants and research organisations
rows.quote: Pharmaceutical manufacturers, applicants and research organizations have to ensure that suspected adverse reactions to their products are reported to the competent authority.
rows.review_note: Review: applicability notes 2009 DRU edition and possible newer BoMRA guidance; RACI accountable set to QPPV/Head of PV equivalent (governance-1) with submissions specialist responsible. Overlaps 0002 (company reporting duty) but kept: different section and wider actor set (applicants, research organisations), hence lifecycle Both. Double-check: quote alone proves actor ('Pharmaceutical manufacturers, applicants and research organizations'), modal ('have to ensure') and the whole statement. Near-duplicate of 0002 (2.4); this row is kept as the primary company reporting duty. No deadline in source. RACI QPPV accountable is the operating-model owner, not named in source.

f.title: Report all suspected reactions for new drugs; serious or unexpected ones for established drugs
f.statement: Section 2.3 lists as reportable: for 'new' drugs, all suspected reactions, including minor ones; for established or well-known drugs, all serious or unexpected (unusual) suspected ADRs. The source does not name who reports.
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked.

rows.actor: Not named in source (2.3 bullets name no actor; per 2.2/2.4, reporters include health professionals and pharmaceutical companies)
rows.quote: For "new" drugs- report all suspected reactions, including minor ones. • For established or well-known drugs- report all serious or unexpected (unusual) suspected ADRs
rows.review_note: Review: actor changed from 'Reporters (healthcare professionals; pharmaceutical companies)' to not-named (the 2.3 bullets name no actor); statement reworded to avoid implying an actor; level Recommended kept (imperative list in a guideline where HCP reporting is voluntary); applicability notes 2009 edition. Double-check: bullet list from 2.3 with no actor and imperative wording in a guideline where HCP reporting is voluntary (2.4); level Recommended is a judgement. Relevant to companies as the reportable-event scope; quote joins bullets.

f.title: Report increased frequency, interactions, special-interest use and withdrawal-associated ADRs
f.statement: Section 2.3 lists as reportable: an observed increased frequency of a given reaction; all suspected ADRs associated with drug-drug, drug-food or drug-food supplement (including herbal or complementary product) interactions; ADRs in special fields of interest such as drug abuse and drug use in pregnancy and during lactation; and suspected ADRs associated with drug withdrawals. The source does not name who reports.
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked.

f.title: Report ADRs from overdose or medication error, lack of efficacy and suspected pharmaceutical defects
f.statement: Section 2.3 lists as reportable: ADRs occurring from overdose or medication error, and cases where there is a lack of efficacy or where suspected pharmaceutical defects are observed. The source does not name who reports.
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked.

f.title: Pharmaceutical companies must report suspected ADRs to the health authorities
f.statement: The reporting of adverse drug reactions is voluntary; however, it is mandatory for pharmaceutical companies to report suspected adverse drug reactions to the health authorities.
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked.

rows.quote: The reporting of adverse drug reactions is voluntary. It is mandatory for pharmaceutical companies to report suspected adverse drug reactions to the health authorities.
rows.review_note: Review: removed '(for healthcare professionals)' from statement, which went beyond the quote (source says only that reporting is voluntary); applicability notes 2009 edition; RACI accountable governance-1. Near-duplicate of 0001 kept (separate section, narrower actor). Double-check: near-duplicate of 0001 (same company reporting duty, 2.4 restates it as 'mandatory'); kept as a draft so an admin can merge or reject it rather than publish two library rows for one obligation. Quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Healthcare professionals: report suspected ADRs, interactions and unusual effects immediately
f.statement: Doctors, nurses and other health professionals are to report any suspected adverse drug reactions, drug interactions and unusual effects immediately.
f.clause: 4 Duties and responsibilities: Doctors, Nurses and other health professionals
f.applicability: Medicines in Botswana under the Drug Regulatory Unit (DRU) Pharmacovigilance Guidelines, 2nd edition, November 2009. This is a 2009 DRU edition; the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) may have issued newer guidance, which should be checked.

f.title: Return completed ADR reporting forms to the National Pharmacovigilance Centre
f.statement: Completed ADR reporting forms must be returned to the National Pharmacovigilance Monitoring Centre, Gaborone.
